description: Default capability for the Coffer desktop window: Tauri's autogenerated `core:default` baseline plus the two window grants the macOS overlay title bar needs (below) and nothing more. The shell's own IPC commands — the daemon-info handshake, the restart, the version-skew check, the interface language the tray is labelled in, the update check and install, and the presence-gated reveal, key backup and approval (each behind its own LocalAuthentication check, spec desktop-app "Release plaintext and approvals only after a presence check in the shell") — are application commands, which the ACL does not gate, so listing them here is not a thing that can be done. Every show/hide/focus/unminimize the shell performs it performs FROM Rust (`tray.rs`, `lib.rs`), which is a direct API call rather than IPC, so a `core:window:allow-show`-style grant buys the webview a reach the shell never uses: `core:window:default` alone leaves the page able to read the window's geometry and unable to move, hide or close it. No dialog or opener permissions either — native file actions go to the daemon over HTTP in both hosts. The notification plugin is registered in `lib.rs` and deliberately granted NOTHING here: the shell raises its own sync alert and approval notification from Rust (`sync_watch.rs`, `approval_watch.rs`; spec vault-sync "Say a vault needs a human where the user already is"), which the ACL does not gate, so listing `notification:default` would only hand the page a banner the shell never asked it to raise. The updater plugin is registered the same way and granted nothing either: the check, the download, the signature verification and the relaunch all run in Rust (`updater.rs`), reached from the page only through the shell's own update commands, so no `updater:` permission belongs here. Two window grants belong to the macOS overlay title bar: `allow-start-dragging` and `allow-toggle-maximize`, which the page's `data-tauri-drag-region` strip needs to move and zoom the window (it has no native title bar to do it).
